history.dynasty: Government of Sikkim project; completed under the patronage of Chief Minister Pawan Kumar Chamling, executed by Kyabje Dodrupchen Rinpoche
history.period: Modern - foundation stone laid by the Dalai Lama on 22 October 1997; construction commenced 1997; consecrated and opened to the public 18 February 2004
history.summary: CSV NAME FLAG: 'Samdruptse Monastery' is a misnomer - this is NOT a monastery. Samdruptse ('wish-fulfilling hill' in the Bhutia language) is the hill near Namchi that hosts the giant 135-foot (45 m, some sources say 147 ft) seated statue of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), the 8th-century saint who introduced Buddhism to the Himalayan region and is revered as Sikkim's patron saint. Conceived as the state government's tribute to Guru Rinpoche and a symbol of Sikkim's Buddhist heritage, the copper statue gilded in gold depicts him holding a vajra and skull cup. The Dalai Lama laid the foundation stone on 22 October 1997, construction began in 1997 under Dodrupchen Rinpoche, the statue was completed in February 2004 and unveiled by Chief Minister Chamling on 18 February 2004 (some sources say November 2004; one travel guide says the inauguration coincided with the 2550th Buddha Jayanti - verify), at an estimated cost of Rs. 4.55 crore. The hill stands at about 2,134 m (7,000 ft) with panoramic views of the Kanchenjunga range; local tradition also holds that the hill is a dormant volcano (unverified). The complex includes prayer wheels, cafes and souvenir shops, and also houses a small Shiva temple, reflecting Sikkim's Hindu-Buddhist religious harmony.

name: Samdruptse (Guru Padmasambhava Statue), Namchi
town_description: Namchi, headquarters of Namchi (South Sikkim) district at about 1,315 m, is a major pilgrimage and tourism centre of Sikkim. Around it lie the Char Dham (Solophok), the Samdruptse Guru Padmasambhava statue, the Sai Mandir at Assangthang, Ngadak and Ralang monasteries, and the Temi Tea Garden - Sikkim's only tea garden.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), West Bengal, approx. 90-100 km from Namchi (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 90-100 km; Siliguri is the road hub.
travel.road: Samdruptse Hill is about 5-7 km from Namchi town (verify); reachable by taxi or shared jeep on a motorable hill road, with a paid parking area at the site.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear skies and Kanchenjunga views; Buddha Purnima (April-May) is the most spiritually significant period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (verify); an entry fee of about Rs. 30 is reported (verify). Circumambulation of the statue with prayer wheels is the customary practice.
